method: Located the original 1900 scanned Italian passages by direct matching of normalized text-layer anchors; inspected six contact sheets holding all 48 distinct source-page images. Printed page offsets were reconciled to actual volume foliation, including Palermo's illustrated leaves where the PDF-page offset changes. Reused stable original observation IDs; no additions to research-observation counts. OCR-normalized anchors are search locators, not facsimile-accurate verbatim quotations.
cautions: St Rosalia historic 1743 five-day pattern cannot automatically be applied as today's annual schedule.
The Cosmas and Damian account expressly references Pitrè's own 1881 book; the two are not independent sources.
Geraci's consecration/blessing language for dairy figurines is local reported testimony, not a verified Roman Ritual formular.
Gangi's alleged Pope Urban VIII correspondence is part of a narrated tradition; the pontifical document remains unread.
Piazza Armerina five/ten/fifteen-year grand feast was irregular, not an annual feast form.
Marineo's processional angel flight involved a child suspended on a line: preserve historical account without suggesting physical reenactment.

records.source_action_or_detail: Three-, four-, and then five-day formats of the historical festino, with the five-day form dated to 1743
Street singers repeat their assigned novena songs for nine consecutive days at the same houses and times
Novena singers collect small payments on the eve of the saint's feast
A documented street-novena verse refers to plague reports from Malta and the saint's attributed protection
The former monumental triumphal cart was constructed in the weeks before the July festival
The cart's wooden carriage was historically taken to the Cala on St John's day before assembly
Cart picture-panels presented episodes of the saint's legendary life, including the hunter's reported discovery
A decorated tier of the historical cart accommodated musicians in ceremonial clothing
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: i musicanti vestiti di gran gala

records.source_action_or_detail: A crowned, white-clad figure of St Rosalia stood high above the historical triumphal cart
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: figura della santa dalle candide vesti

records.source_action_or_detail: Smaller allegorical carts were paraded along the Cassaro and Strada Nuova on consecutive days
Bareback horse races were held on the second through fourth days in the older festival programme
An older practice of racing horses ridden by poor foundling jockeys was abandoned in favour of riderless racing
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: fantini in carne e in ossa

records.source_action_or_detail: An 1895 petition requested restoration of the older five-day municipal festino and its spectacles
A restored triumphal cart travelled via Via Libertà in the 1896 celebration rather than the earlier Cassaro route
Cathedral solemn Vespers shifted from the fourth festival day to the second in Pitrè's period
The Cathedral was densely illuminated for Vespers in the historical festival
The city commissioned a large scenographic fireworks display with a selected theme
Spectators watched the fireworks from boats in the gulf adorned with canopies and coloured lanterns
A rocket signalled the mayor's cue to begin the fireworks display
Named confraternities made public wax offerings; a chaplain said Mass in the saint's chapel for them
The last-day procession involved St Rosalia's relics together with confraternities, clergy and civic representatives
Confraternity platforms representing other patron saints preceded St Rosalia's silver reliquary
The municipality customarily printed the order of participating confraternities and clergy for the procession
The reliquary route alternated groups of Palermo quarters between successive years
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: quartieri dell albergarla e della kalsa

records.source_action_or_detail: The relic procession ran from the evening of 15 July into the early hours of the following day
A municipal master mason used a bell to signal halts in the procession
Mason bearers advanced the reliquary with a deliberate side-to-side carrying gait
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: un passo a destra ed uno a sinistra

records.source_action_or_detail: Pitrè distinguishes restrictions on the public procession from continuation of the feast inside the church
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: la festa si ripete in chiesa

records.source_action_or_detail: The public exit of the saints' statues was restored after repeated fishermen's petitions
The church displayed numerous votive tablets recounting injuries and reported favours
Donors' votive offerings were moved to make space and small devotional images supplied in response to alms
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: tabelle tutte piu o meno simili

records.source_action_or_detail: Petitioners used a vernacular invocation addressing the paired saints as healers
Festival vendors sold edible saints' figurines and confectionery at makeshift stalls
Children played with cane tubes used to blow small hackberry fruits during the feast market
The saint-day stalls displayed early seasonal quinces, pomegranates, carobs and other fruit
A local belief discouraged engaged girls from accepting quinces as gifts because of an omen of quarrels
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: delle cotogne che a nessun patto

records.source_action_or_detail: Ornately assembled fruit stalls included watercolour scenes of the saints' procession and martyrdom
Festival visitors took home distinctive first fruits bought at the saint-day market
Fishermen and their families travelled from the fishing quarters and nearby communities for the statues' exit
Fishermen attributed expected rain to the saints during a period of drought
A sudden ringing of church bells announced the emergence of the saints' statues
Statue bearers ran towards the Cathedral for the first stop, honouring St Rosalia's relics
Pitrè refers to an older 1748 monastery privilege relevant to routes of municipal processions; original document not read here
The portable statues were carried in running movements towards the Capuchinelle area
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: prender la rincorsa e volare verso

records.source_action_or_detail: Fishermen and fishmongers of the Kalsa were privileged to carry the saints' heavy litter
The litter bearers wore white clothing, a red waist sash, a yellow headscarf and bare feet
A disabled child was placed briefly on the litter and devotional torches were offered
Two congregations led hundreds of children carrying small flower-topped water jugs
Infants associated with healing vows were dressed in the saints' festival costume by their mothers
Some devotees attributed healing powers to the children's water jugs after the procession; no blessing verified
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: acqua dei nostri piccolini dopo la processione

records.source_action_or_detail: Participants danced, turned and performed acrobatic movements before the statues
The route headed towards coastal fishing districts rather than gardens visited by other saints' processions
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: cosi i ss cosimo e damiano si conducono verso il mare

records.source_action_or_detail: The procession followed the old city walls towards the Castello and fishing communities
The saints' litter was spun repeatedly in rapid circles in the Kalsa district
Devotees handed cloths and other articles to a cleric for touching to the statues, later treating them as protective objects; formal blessing unverified
The statues returned to their church around midnight accompanied by bells
A local foundation tradition linked the Marian banner to Count Roger; treated by Pitrè as transmitted legend
A reported discovery of the hidden banner followed episcopally permitted public supplication according to an older historian cited by Pitrè
The Marian banner was covered with worked silver and devotional jewels
The extraordinary 'festa grande' was described as recurring on irregular cycles of five, ten or fifteen years rather than every August
The more elaborate Assumption celebration lasted five days and included civic races and bands
A ceremonial horse cavalcade represented Count Roger's entry, with a senior participant carrying a copy of the banner
The last-day procession carried the Marian banner behind confraternities and their standing patron-saint statues
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: il vessillo vien condotto in giro

records.source_action_or_detail: Carriage of the decorated Marian banner had a locally restricted social privilege
Pitrè reports a historical succession of banner-carrier privilege from clergy to municipal jurats
An older triumphal car travelled with the decorated Marian throne
Before suppression of religious houses, nuns arranged temporary altars as stopping places and hosted civic representatives
In the annual procession a senior lawyer announced stops using a silver bell
A procession included a piece of the Holy Cross associated with the church of the Holy Spirit.
Nine confraternities participated, said to number roughly four hundred members each in the described observance.
Residents of Gangi made pilgrimage to the sanctuary of the Holy Spirit.
An orally transmitted discovery story alleged a consultation with Pope Urban VIII about a rock image; no original pontifical document inspected.
The Holy Spirit celebration fell at Pentecost after seven preceding Thursdays treated as separate festival observances.
Sixteen strong men carried a life-size image of St James on their shoulders beneath its small canopy.
The patron's image stopped at each household seeking offerings in money, grain, beans, oil, wine or eggs.
The image was held at a home until an offering had been received, accompanied by acclamations and music.
The collectors carried the image through steep and difficult streets throughout the settlement.
The image also visited rural growers who wanted the patron's presence among orchards and gardens.
Garden owners expected trampled vegetation to regrow especially vigorously; this is a reported folk belief, not a verified blessing.
Visitors offered selected grape clusters, tying them to the silver staff of the saint's image.
Bearers were supplied with wine from small barrels during the rounds.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: ai portatori del fercolo si offre del vino

records.source_action_or_detail: When passing the Franciscan convent the bearers ran the saint's image across its square towards the church door.
People explained the convent visit by calling St Francis a blood relative of St James; a folk explanation, not established genealogy.
The third Sunday of each month honoured the Blessed Sacrament under sponsorship of a different local social or occupational group.
The third Sunday of June was assigned to shepherds, whose celebration uniquely featured a mounted cavalcade.
Morning bells announced Exposition of the Sacrament, a solemn Mass and preaching for the shepherds' observance.
Households prepared festival gifts by milking their animals and cooking a soft dairy mixture.
A piece of the dairy paste was reportedly sprinkled in the home with holy water using an olive branch, salted and preserved in glass.
The preserved dairy piece was believed to protect livestock for a year; efficacy not endorsed or verified.
The remaining dairy paste was modelled into birds, little horses and other figurines for children.
A local belief alleged children required a festival toy horse for a good year; not an endorsed religious teaching.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: non passera bene tutto l anno

records.source_action_or_detail: A trumpet signal announced the shepherds' mounted procession after the traditional midday waiting point.
Shepherds entered the town on ornamented riding animals dressed in their best or new clothing.
A trumpeter and band headed paired riders, with younger participants preceding elders.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: a due a due si avanzano

records.source_action_or_detail: Younger shepherds carried ribboned umbrella-shaped frames holding small animal-shaped caciocavalli.
Older shepherds carried ribbon-tied bunches of wax instead of the dairy display frames.
At town squares youths recited occasional verses honouring the Eucharist as the cavalcade passed under arches and falling flowers.
At the Cathedral the riders dismounted and entered to fulfil their vow with wax offerings and seek a blessing.
Blessed dairy figurines were apportioned among relatives and friends as devotional gifts; approving minister and formula unverified.
Pitrè reports an archiepiscopally ordered shift of the annual feast to the penultimate Sunday of August, with three days of celebration.
The St Cyrus celebration distinguished its first-day and second-day public processions.
A large first-day procession brought devotees bearing individually lighted candles.
Confraternities marched with banners differentiated by their habit colours.
Drummers accompanying confraternal standards wore white hoods and garments with coloured mantles.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: tamburini in abito e cappuccio bianco

records.source_action_or_detail: The banners of St Michael, the Blessed Sacrament and Holy Souls were distinguished by different reported colours and lengths.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: varia di colore e di lunghezza

records.source_action_or_detail: Women participated in festive clothing while walking barefoot.
The final litter held a silver urn said to contain the saint's skull relic; carrying privileges were locally restricted.
Participants behind the litter repeated a vernacular invocation seeking St Cyrus's help.
On the second day a mounted company brought offerings donated by devotees over the past year.
A banner sent by emigrants in America was added to the mounted offering procession.
At a designated procession halt a costumed child playing an angel was carried along a rope toward the statue, recited a hymn or prayer, and withdrew.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: vestito da angelo per un anello

records.source_action_or_detail: An intermittently assembled triumphal cart portrayed an apotheosis of the saint and carried his image.
The triumphal cart could accommodate large numbers of participants, including two musical bands and people seeking favours.
Eight oxen and fancifully costumed drivers hauled the triumphal cart through the principal streets.
The costly cart procession was substituted for, rather than staged together with, the large Dimostranza spectacle.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: carro trionfale si costruisce di tanto

records.source_action_or_detail: The Dimostranza presented scenes of a saint's life in public streets and squares using local, nonprofessional performers.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: sulle pubbliche vie e sulle piazze

records.source_action_or_detail: The Marineo spectacle was said to use roughly four hundred characters under the direction of a priest.
The street performance moved through Marineo from late morning until approximately five in the afternoon.
The sacred dramatization included mounted and walking figures representing soldiers, hermits, angels, demons and personified virtues and vices.
Costumed actors paused at selected open spaces to perform successive episodes from the life of St Cyrus.
records.italian_normalized_text_anchor: i personaggi si fermano a gruppi

records.source_action_or_detail: The performer playing the devil moved apart between scenes before returning to tempt the young saint and contest the angel.
